name: base
summary: Every machine gets safety rules, the model table, and the jobs that keep it current.
day: Agents ask before they break things, pick the right model for each task, and every machine is up to date when you start.
cost: You set up nothing. Every Hedge machine gets it.
risk: Hedge owns its hooks in Claude Code and Codex. Hedge keeps a hook that you wrote yourself on the same event until you adopt Hedge's.

settings.question: Which GitHub repo, such as you/context, holds what your agents learn and record: memory, notes, maps, and logs? Share it with your team, but keep it private. Hedge takes the memory, library, map, and log settings from it unless you set them.
Which folder holds the checkout of your context repo?
Which analytics host receives Hedge's usage events? Give its capture URL, such as https://us.i.posthog.com.
Which project key does that analytics host take the events with? A PostHog project key starts with phc_.
Which agent runtime starts your threads and runs scheduled agent prompts? Give the runtime's name, such as t3 or herdr. Hedge turns on the pack that brings it.

workflows.name: Agent rules
workflows.sentence: Agents confirm destructive actions, keep private data out of public repos, and pick the right model for each task.

workflows.name: Nightly updates
workflows.sentence: Hedge, your profile, Claude Code, Codex, their plugins, and T3 Code update themselves every night. T3 Code waits until no agent turn runs. A failed update tries again each hour until 05:47 UTC.

workflows.name: Fresh skills
workflows.sentence: Every five minutes, Hedge asks each pack source that follows a branch, such as your skills repository, whether it moved. When it moved forward, Hedge updates the skills, guides, and instructions it brings. A source you edited, such as a changed skill, and a rewritten branch wait for you. Everything else waits for the nightly update.

workflows.name: Worktree cleanup
workflows.sentence: Every few minutes, Hedge removes idle worktrees whose work has merged.

workflows.name: Disk guard
workflows.sentence: Agents check free disk before big jobs and run builds and tests in a capped slot, so one job cannot fill or freeze a devbox.

workflows.name: Usage events
workflows.sentence: Hedge counts how often you and your agents run its commands and recall memory, and sends the counts to your own analytics project every five minutes.
workflows.risk: Command names, counts, and the machine name leave the machine for the analytics project you name. Arguments, prompts, file contents, and secrets never do.

workflows.name: Format on edit
workflows.sentence: After Claude or Codex edits a file, the repository's own lint-staged formatters and fixers rewrite it, and the agent sees what they could not fix.
workflows.risk: It runs after every edit in every repository, before you review the change, not only at commit. It runs only known formatters (Prettier, Biome, ESLint, Ruff, gofmt, shfmt and a few more) that the repository's lint-staged config names, with only their own rewrite and check flags, from the repository's installed node_modules/.bin or your PATH. It never runs package runners such as bunx or npx, interpreters, shells, scripts, Git, or a file the repository commits, also through a symlink, and no installed formatter runs when the repository commits anything under node_modules. Formatters and the tools they start see only PATH entries outside the repository. Formatters whose config can be code, such as ESLint and Prettier, run only once the repository's packages are installed, and no formatter runs from your PATH in a repository that pins tool versions for a version manager. An installed formatter still loads the repository's own config, and some configs, such as eslint.config.js, are code.

check: case "$(readlink "$HOME/.local/bin/codex")" in "$HOME"/.local/share/fleet/*) exit 1 ;; esac; exec codex --version
